newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Chidambaram says bank lending will pick up.
newsitem.headline: India's Chidambaram says bank lending will pick up.

text.p: Indian Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said on Monday that he believed bank lending would pick up.
"I think that banks will begin to lend now," Chidambaram told reporters as he left a meeting with Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor C. Rangarajan.
Chidambaram told Reuters on Saturday that he wanted to discuss the flow of bank credit to non-farm sectors with Rangarajan. "The governor (Rangarajan) is in constant touch with the banks," he said.
Rangarajan told reporters that the RBI had been absorbing the excess supply of foreign currency by adding to reserves and preventing the appreciation of the rupee against the U.S. dollar.

"But over the next few months we will see how the foreign currency assets move and take a decision as we go along because the impact of foreign exchange assets is on the reserve money which will further lead to money supply," he said.

The RBI chief said that in the current 1996/97 (April-March) financial year, foreign exchange assets had increased but net RBI credit to the federal government, or Centre, had fallen, leaving reserve money in balance.
"So we will watch both net RBI credit to the Centre as well as foreign exchange assets," he said.

"If we find foreign exchange inflow is of such an order that the targeted rate of growth in the money supply will be breached, then we will take the open market operation to sterilise the increase," Rangarajan said.
The RBI governor said the cash reserve ratio (CRR) had been brought down to below 10 percent from very high levels.
Asked how far the CRR would fall, he said: "You'll have to wait until the 15th of April." He was referring to the date on which the RBI is expected to announce its new credit policy.
